pre_actions.comment: Choose International locale to avoid geo-redirect
Ensure English language if locale modal appears

code_hints: After navigation, first try to click the cookie consent (#onetrust-accept-btn-handler) and any International/English locale button if present, then wait for network idle.
If PLP tiles are still missing, perform incremental scroll (e.g., window.scrollBy) until any of the product tile selectors becomes visible or until max steps reached.
When extracting product links, restrict to anchors under detected product tiles and normalize to absolute URLs; prefer those containing '/en-int/' to avoid locale flips.
On PDP, if price/title selectors fail, parse the first JSON-LD block (application/ld+json) for offers.price and name as a fallback.
Set Accept-Language header to en-GB to reduce locale modals; persist locale choice via cookies/localStorage only if your framework allows safe writes.
If a full-screen locale modal is detected (dialog with country/language content), attempt clicking a control containing 'International' then 'English'. Retry wait for grid afterward.
Use a longer initial wait for PLP (up to 20s or until grid selector appears) as the site lazy-loads content after hydration.
rationale: The failure likely stems from a locale/cookie gate and a malformed URL with duplicate locale segments (/en-gb/en-int/) that can trigger redirects and prevent the PLP grid from rendering. Adding robust wait selectors and pre-actions to accept cookies and pick the International/English locale should unblock rendering. The PLP on moncler commonly lazy-loads tiles; enabling incremental scroll and longer waits helps materialize product cards. PDP extraction includes flexible price/title selectors plus a JSON-LD fallback for resiliency. URL normalization ensures consistent use of /en-int/ and avoids misnavigation to monclergroup.com.
